editorial:
Imagine moving to Long Island and finding out your neighbor is a millionaire who throws the wildest parties you have ever seen. That is exactly what happens to Nick, a normal guy who gets pulled into the flashy world of Jay Gatsby. You will see a story about a man who has everything but still feels empty because he is chasing a love from his past. The vibe is very old-school and classy, making you feel like you are stepping back into a time of fancy suits and huge mansions where everyone has a secret they are trying to hide.

The acting is solid and keeps you interested in the drama between the couples. While some parts might feel a bit slow compared to modern films, the tension builds up nicely. If you love a good story about lost love and rich people making bad choices, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a restored version to get the best picture.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Gatsby takes the blame for a car accident that killed Myrtle. This leads to a heartbroken and angry man tracking him down and shooting Gatsby in his pool. In the end, you see that almost nobody who enjoyed Gatsby's parties actually cared about him. Nick is the only one who stays to help with the funeral, showing how lonely Gatsby really was despite all his money.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood stories and tragic romances.
